utterances.text: You do not discount the fact that the velocity of a mortar could be important to analysis based on the fact that the speed increases as the number of charges increase?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just a few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, any further questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just a few. We should be able to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, at temporary transcript page of 69 through 70, you were asked about the impact of the shelling on the civilian population of Sarajevo. What impact was there upon both the civilian population and from the shelling from the use of civilian buildings for military purposes like the basement that you identified with the two floors being used for military purposes? Do you believe that that had any impact?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: It was the -- all fighting factions would either put their base place -- base plates close to a civilian complex, for example, in the parking lot of a hospital or next to a UN battalion, for example. And in this case, when visiting for that mortar round, this was a building with predominantly civilian people living in there with only a few floors being used by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were asked about the compass that you used to perform your analysis. Could you please give us a little bit more details about the specific type of compass and what kind of settings it had on it.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: It's a -- to the best of my recollection it's a Silva compass. It's issued by the Canadian Armed Forces. It's a compass used throughout my army. It's similar to any outdoor compass that you can find. It's graduated in mils and in degrees. And it has a setting for magnetic declination which I applied on that compass for the area I was in during my one year in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you were shown a number of UNMO sitreps by the Prosecution. Did your job as military assistant to Mr. de Mello include any duties in relation to UNMO reporting in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No. I did not -- for the time I worked for Mr. de Mello in Sarajevo, I reported to him only.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And you were shown portions of your testimony from the Karadzic case by the Prosecution. Having reviewed those, does that change anything from your statement or do you stand by the statement as written? When I say "statement," the statement that you signed in 2011.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: I stand by that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And last question: You were asked about not knowing whether it was an 82- or 120-millimetre mortar. Are there any differences in terms of doing crater analysis between an 82- and 120-millimetre mortar in terms of the methodology used?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No, it's the same process.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Major, I thank you for answering my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, unless you have anything further, I have no further questions for the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have perhaps a few questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few times you say whether you had the feeling or that you reported that a shell could have been fired from within BiH-held territory or from outside. What did you take as the distance to the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: I never measured it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you drew conclusions on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: On the calculations I concluded that I couldn't tell which one, which side fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But what was the distance from the confrontation line to the Markale market? So where did BiH territory or BiH-held territory become Serbian-held territory?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: I can't -- I looked at my map. It's about -- I don't know the exact distance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: 2000-some odd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we just looked at the firing tables and apart from wind, elevation, et cetera, we came close to 5 kilometres for the range of the mortars described in those tables. You earlier said the tables you used -- well, they were not the same but there wasn't that much of a difference. Now, I'm trying to understand that because if those tables were slightly different, I would say, well, 5 kilometres might be 4 and a half or even 4, but you'd have to come down in your own estimate to 2 kilometres. And even if it were 2 and a half kilometres, then there's not a slight difference but there's a pretty big difference. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: Yes, I would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And ever puzzled by what made these tables to be so different from the --

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No, I was never puzzled. But certainly when you look at the direction, the direction is all forward-sloping, and you don't put a mortar base plate on a forward slope tactically. You hide it behind a hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any BiH-held territory in that direction hidden behind the hill?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your feeling or your ideas are that you wouldn't put a mortar there in that direction because it's uphill and you just told me that that's not where you would put a mortar.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: That is correct. It's all forward-sloping for a long time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Until the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: Beyond the confrontation line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean that the hill continues beyond the confrontation line being uphill?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I'm not suggesting anything, but have you ever thought about including that in your subject opinion, because it's new me. I never saw -- I saw it nowhere in your analysis or in your statement.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No, it's not in my analysis because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not an analysis you would say.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No. I only later in my life, as I go through this, drew a line on that bearing and looked at the terrain. You can see it on Google Earth. You know, the terrain is sloping up all the time. As you leave the city, it's starts to go up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you never thought when you reviewed your statement to say: Well, this certainly is all the truth because that's what I wrote, that's what I reported, that's what I said. But there's another truth that I meanwhile concluded - and again, I'm not trying to seduce you to any conclusions - but meanwhile I got the impression that you would never put a mortar on such a slope.

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: That's correct. You don't put mortars on forward slopes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you didn't consider that to be relevant enough when reviewing your statement to add to it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No. I considered just the angle -- the direction and the angle of descent and all that information, to the best of my recollection, applied that to the range tables, and wrote my report, and concluded that between range 1 and 6, I couldn't tell you who fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that's all well understood, as I said. You attested to that's the truth, that's what you reported, these were the reasons. Did it ever come to your mind that your new developed views on whether it would be logical, for example, to put a mortar there might be relevant for this claim to know as well?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, my apologies. I forgot to tender the tables that I used. If I, at this time, could please tender 65 ter 33075 into evidence. And they're the full tables related to the applicable mortar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33075 receives Exhibit Number P7539, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It's admitted into evidence. And I have one more question for you. The tables you did use, do you still have copies of those tables?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At home?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any way that you could provide them to the Victims and Witness Section so that they can be copied and that the Chamber is in a position to verify whether your calculations at the time were accurate and would bring you within the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: My understanding is if that request is done through the channels that are used, I will be directed by my country and -- to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Thank you. So you're willing. And again also keep them well --

utterances.speaker: JOHN RUSSELL
utterances.text: They're with the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then if -- with the diary. If there's any need that they're still there. No further questions. Mr. Russell, this concludes your evidence in this court. I would like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the Bench, put to you by the parties, primarily the parties and only secondarily the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the Chamber had a subjective feeling of rumours that there would be problems in having witnesses for the whole of the week. Is that -- and is there any accuracy in those rumours?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon the current estimates, I think we should have witnesses for this whole week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For this whole week. That is good to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Next one is the one that is not confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, next week. Perhaps that is part of the rumours. And you know that whenever I hear a rumour, I immediately put it somewhere on the record to seek whether it is just rumour or whether it is anything more. We adjourn for the day, and we resume tomorrow, the 8th of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this very same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 8th day of September, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.12 p.m.,
